briefing.question: Does bitcoin hold the mid-$60,000s into the weekly close, or does dealer hedging and forced selling carry it lower in thin overnight trade?

lead.headline: Bitcoin slips under $64,000 in second wave of weekend selling
lead.standfirst: The world's largest cryptocurrency set a fresh three-month low on Saturday evening, with Zcash falling twice as fast, as options positioning threatened to exaggerate swings.
body: Bitcoin fell below $64,000 on Kraken shortly after 21:00 UK time on Saturday, touching about $63,854, its lowest level since August. It traded near $64,490 at 21:30 UK, down about 5.5% over 24 hours.

The fall came after a brief early-evening bounce to about $66,100 faded. CoinDesk reported the coin was down about 13.5% on the week, with ether down 18%, and that it had slipped nearly 3% since US stock markets closed on Friday.

Options positioning may be adding to the swings. CoinDesk, citing Greeks.Live data, reported that dealers were net short gamma between roughly $58,000 and $72,000, meaning their hedging tends to sell into falls and buy into rallies. Hedging only turns calming above about $73,000.
Zcash fell harder than bitcoin. It briefly touched about $801 on Kraken and traded near $826, down about 11.5% over 24 hours, having held up better earlier in the week.

Glassnode analyst James Check told CoinDesk the slide was the fourth capitulation wave since bitcoin's all-time high, with many sellers having bought in the $80,000s in September. He said prices were in a 'deep value' zone but stressed that did not mean the bottom was in.
Attention now turns to the weekly close at midnight UK and Monday's US spot ETF flows, after two weeks of outflows totalling $2.35 billion.

headline: Bitcoin slid below $64,000 this evening, a new three-month low, after an early bounce faded. Zcash fell about 11.5% on the day, touching $801.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, evening edition. Bitcoin fell below sixty-four thousand dollars just after nine o'clock UK time, a new three-month low, after a brief bounce earlier in the evening faded. It is down about five and a half percent today and around fifteen percent on the week. Zcash fell harder, briefly touching about eight hundred dollars, down around eleven percent today. Options data suggests dealer hedging could exaggerate moves either way between fifty-eight and seventy-two thousand dollars. Watch the weekly close at midnight and Monday's fund flows. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Bitcoin slips under $64,000 to a fresh three-month low
stories.why: Since the afternoon edition bitcoin bounced to about $66,100 around 17:00 UK, then fell again after 20:00 UK to a low near $63,854 on Kraken. It traded near $64,490 at 21:30 UK, down about 5.5% over 24 hours. CoinDesk put the weekly fall at about 13.5%.
stories.caveat: Weekly change depends on the start point: about 13.5% in CoinDesk, about 15% measured from $75,750 on 7 November.

note.read: A failed bounce followed by a lower low suggests selling has not exhausted itself, even after Friday's and this afternoon's liquidations.
note.alt: Saturday night liquidity is very thin; a small amount of selling can print a new low that is reclaimed once Asian and US markets reopen.
note.change: A weekly close back above about $65,500 to $66,000 and a turn to ETF inflows on Monday would weaken the bearish read.

stories.title: Zcash falls about 11.5% on the day, briefly touching $801
stories.why: At the afternoon edition Zcash was near $861. It fell with bitcoin after 20:00 UK, touching about $801 on Kraken, and traded near $826 at 21:30 UK, down about 11.5% over 24 hours against bitcoin's 5.5%.

note.read: Zcash is now behaving like a higher-beta version of bitcoin rather than the relative safe spot it was earlier in the week.
note.alt: Zcash's earlier outperformance may simply be unwinding; the fall could reflect profit-taking on its own rally rather than fresh bad news.
note.change: Holding above $800 on another bitcoin dip would suggest the round number is acting as support.

stories.title: Options dealers' hedging may amplify swings between $58,000 and $72,000
stories.why: CoinDesk, citing Greeks.Live, reported that bitcoin options dealers were net short gamma across a range of roughly $58,000 to $72,000, so their hedging tends to add to falls and rallies. Positioning only turns stabilising above about $73,000, leaving bitcoin inside the volatile zone.
stories.caveat: Gamma estimates come from one data provider and shift as options are traded and expire.

stories.title: Glassnode analyst calls the slide a fourth capitulation wave
stories.why: James Check told CoinDesk that many recent sellers bought in the $80,000s in September and are now selling at a loss, the fourth such wave since the all-time high. He said prices had reached a 'deep value' zone last seen in February and late June, but that this did not mark a bottom.

stories.title: No new ETF data until Monday after $2.35 billion two-week outflow
stories.why: Nothing new since the afternoon edition. The Block also reported US spot bitcoin funds lost about $1 billion for a second straight week. Monday's figures will show whether the weekend fall drew more withdrawals.

stories.title: Bank of England tests blockchain-linked FX settlement with Singapore and Thailand
stories.why: CoinDesk reported Project Meridian FX APAC tested payment-versus-payment settlement across conventional and blockchain systems. The Bank of England plans a live synchronisation interface in 2028, a sign of its slow, infrastructure-first approach to tokenised money.

explained.title: What negative gamma means
body: Banks and trading firms that sell options hedge their risk by buying or selling the underlying coin. When they are 'short gamma', the hedge forces them to sell more as the price falls and buy more as it rises.

That makes moves bigger in both directions while the price stays inside the affected range. When dealers are 'long gamma' the opposite happens: they buy dips and sell rallies, which tends to calm the market.

investigating: Does the selling exhaust itself overnight? Evidence: the bitcoin weekly close at midnight UK and Sunday's liquidation totals.
Will ETF outflows extend to a third week? Evidence: Farside and SoSoValue figures for Monday 16 November.
Is Zcash's sharper fall about bitcoin or about Zcash? Evidence: whether ZEC keeps underperforming if bitcoin steadies on Sunday.
